Exploratory, pre-registered test of whether changes at the ice–bed boundary (basal water pressure, uplift, bed tilt) occur before glacier acceleration, on the one event observed with basal pressure at Langhovde Glacier, East Antarctica (2–6 January 2022). It follows a reproduction of Sugiyama et al. (2026), [doi:10.1038/s41467-026-72724-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-72724-x).

**Result: inconclusive.**
- Rain led the basal pressure rise by about 19 h.
- The order of pressure and acceleration is not resolved, by ± 10 h.
- Kinematic 1 s GNSS shows a ~12 h trunk motion larger than the event's speed-up.
- The proposed multi-event predictive test needs more events than the record contains.

This release contains:
- the data-download, kinematic GNSS processing (RTKLIB) and analysis notebooks, with a Snakemake pipeline and pixi environment;
- the pre-registered analysis plan with dated amendments;
- the results tables and figures;
- draft FORRT nanopublications.

Data:
- the deposit [doi:10.17632/8wvtxg53ry.1](https://doi.org/10.17632/8wvtxg53ry.1);
- NIPR Arctic Data archive System records A20220506-001, -002 and -004 (CC BY 4.0).

The code reuses [doi:10.5281/zenodo.23257925](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23257925).

The research question was proposed by an external researcher. The code was developed by the author with an AI coding agent.

Cite as described in `CITATION.cff`.
